root_idea.summary: The root centers on binding or encircling one thing with another, whether lengthwise or around it.
root_idea.development: From binding and twisting develop the senses of sinews and compactness, objects or people gathered into a cohesive group, attachment and surrounding, and figurative severity or constriction.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized adjective عَصِيب.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, it describes a day in the expression يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ. The lexical explanation allows either an active sense, “causing distress,” or a resultative sense, “hemmed in or made severe.”

senses.definition: A cohesive group or company whose members are bound together and support one another.
senses.usage_conditions: A collective noun; classical descriptions vary in the number, and the word can be used of groups of people and other beings. The Quranic contexts present a mutually joined company rather than imposing a fixed numerical limit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To twist, wind, fold, bind, or tie something; to wrap or draw together threads, a wound, a body part, tree branches, or a cracked vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The primary concrete sense; the binding may be lengthwise or around an object, and may involve several turns or a cord.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind the testicles of a male animal so that they fall without extraction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized practice described of rams, goats, and other animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind a she-camel’s thighs or the lower parts of her nostrils in order to make her yield milk copiously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The physical restraint is also the basis of the figurative expression “to give by force.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compel or extract something by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of binding, especially said of forcing a camel or person to yield.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw people together and make an affair severe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an event or circumstance that gathers people and becomes hard or intense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attach, attribute, or impose something upon someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively of attaching disgrace to a person or binding obligations upon someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To grasp or seize something with the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be an opponent seized in combat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cling or keep closely to something or a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of staying by water or remaining in one’s house or tent without leaving it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To surround, encompass, or assemble around something or someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can describe people gathering around a person for fighting or defense, camels encircling water, or relations encompassing a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become dry through saliva adhering and drying in the mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of saliva or the mouth, especially in thirst or fear; the mouth may consequently become foul or coated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become very hungry, with the bowels nearly dried by hunger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense is associated with the practice of binding the belly because of hunger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the horizon, to become red.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of the horizon’s appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have much sinew or tendon; of flesh, sinewy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes flesh or meat containing many sinews.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become firm and compact in flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A description of flesh or bodily make that is tightly knit rather than flabby.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind or wind something around with repeated turns; especially to turban or bandage the head, a broken limb, or a wound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived form emphasizes repeated wrapping or the causative act of making something bound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone a chief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from crowning or binding a turban around the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or wound someone at the place of the turban with a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized idiomatic construction referring to the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone hungry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Drought or sterile years may be the agent of the hunger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of drought or adverse fortune, to consume a person’s property or livestock and thereby destroy him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The loss of property leaves the person in the condition of one made hungry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A poor or needy person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A person whose milk-producing livestock or property has become scarce may be called this.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a female count as an ʿaṣabah through her association with a male.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized kinship and legal-social usage describing consociation with the male side.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind or wind a turban or bandage around one’s own head or body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reflexive derived form describes self-wrapping, including binding the body because of hunger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind one’s body with cloth because of hunger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction refers to the customary hunger-bandage around the belly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be made a chief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quasi-passive extension of the act of crowning or turbaning a chief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To show party zeal, support one’s group, or league with others in its defense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The group may be defended whether it is wronged or wrongful; the sense includes summoning others to join the alliance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become content with something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with the preposition بِـ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become hard, firm, or strong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical explanation is brief but presents intensification or hardening as the verb’s sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To place a turban or crown around one’s own head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a turban or crown as the encircling object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To form or collect oneself into a company or companies.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb describes people becoming organized into groups called ʿuṣbah or ʿiṣābah.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect together into companies or form one cohesive company.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people or other groups becoming gathered into a collective body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exert oneself or strive in traveling or moving at a fast pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of people or camels journeying together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become vehement, severe, or concentrated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a day or of evil that intensifies and becomes severe.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A Yemeni fabric whose yarn is gathered or bound, dyed, and then woven.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The binding leaves some portions undyed, producing a variegated or striped textile; the term may also denote the garment itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A red cloud or mist seen in the western horizon, especially in a time of drought.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also applied to clouds resembling a particular smeared or streaked formation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A material used for beads, necklaces, or handles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The material is variously identified as cut animal tendons or, in a Yemeni report, the teeth or bones of a sea animal; the precise referent is uncertain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Saliva that has adhered and dried in the mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the dried substance, also used figuratively in an expression for dying.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A light, active, sharp-headed boy or young man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An archaic personal description; it is not the ordinary adjective for physical strength.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A twining plant that winds around other trees, especially the plant called لَبْلَاب.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related feminine forms عُصْبَة and عَصْبَة may denote the individual plant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tenacious person, especially one difficult to dislodge in wrestling or grappling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative comparison to a twining plant that clings tightly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sinews, tendons, or ligaments that connect and bind the joints; by extension, nerves in some usages.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun for the connective structures of humans and animals; the singular feminine form may denote one such structure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The best or outstanding members of a people or party.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective or plural-valued figurative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man’s people or paternal-side party who league together for his defense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This social-kinship sense concerns the group supporting a person and is distinct from the general Quranic noun for a company.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An agnatic heir who receives what remains after the specified inheritance shares, or the heirs collectively entitled in that way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical inheritance term for paternal male relations and, in certain legal cases, a single person or woman; the legal applications vary by case.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A partisan: one who supports or defends his people or party and is zealous on its behalf.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can include a person who summons others to join the party or league.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Partisanship, party spirit, or zealous attachment to a group and its shared interest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may describe the strong bond holding several people together by a common interest or opinion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cord used to bind a she-camel’s thigh so that she will yield milk copiously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized implement associated with the milking practice described under the verb عَصَبَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that will not yield much milk until her thigh or thighs, or sometimes the lower parts of her nostrils, are bound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The binding is performed before or during milking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman with little flesh in the buttocks and thighs, or light hips.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized physical description of a woman’s build.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A preparation of animal intestines twisted, folded, and bound together, or lights bound with intestines and roasted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of sheep’s or goats’ intestines and related food preparations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A band, fillet, bandage, or turban used to bind or wind around the head or another part of the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote a small head covering, a turban, or a bandage for a wound or broken limb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A crown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from a head-band or turban that encircles the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller or spinner of thread or yarn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A professional designation linked to the binding and handling of thread.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a mouth dried by the drying of saliva.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used predicatively of the mouth or as an adjective for a man in that condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hungry, especially one who has bound his waist or belly because of hunger; hence needy or poor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The binding may involve cloth and, according to some descriptions, a stone under the bandage; the lexical sense also extends to one whose property has been consumed by drought.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Turbaned or attired with a turban.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive description of someone whose head has been wrapped.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chief, or one made a chief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive extension from being crowned or turbaned.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Crowned, especially a crowned king.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The crown is understood as encircling the head like a turban.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Twisted, wound around, folded tightly, or bound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of something subjected to the concrete act of عَصَبَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firmly and compactly built in flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a bodily make that is tightly knit and not flabby.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slender or elegant sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of tightness or slender compact form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hungry, with the belly bound; by extension, very hungry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is associated with binding the belly because of hunger and is also used in a dialectal sense simply for hungry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A letter or written message.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on a letter being tied or bound with thread or string.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strong or sturdy man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An archaic personal epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mode or manner of binding or winding a turban or the like around the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical noun for the manner in which the head is bound or wound.
